feedback.problem:
The line $y=8x-1$ intersects the curve $y=\frac{1}{2x}-1$ at the points $A(-\frac{1}{4},-3)$ and $B.$ Find the coordinates of $B.$

The coordinates of $B$ are $($
{{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=8x-1 \\ y=\frac{1}{2x}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}8x-1 & =\frac{1}{2x}-1 \\ 8x & =\frac{1}{2x} \\ 16{x}^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =\frac{1}{16} \\ x & =\pm \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points are $x=-\frac{1}{4}$ and $x=\frac{1}{4}.$ To find the $y$-coordinates of the intersection points, we plug these values into either curve. Let's choose the second equation.

- Substituting $x=-\frac{1}{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =8x-1 \\  & =8(-\frac{1}{4})-1 \\  & =-2-1 \\  & =-3,\end{aligned}
$$

so one point of intersection is $(-\frac{1}{4},-3).$

- Substituting $x=\frac{1}{4},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =8x-1 \\  & =8(\frac{1}{4})-1 \\  & =2-1 \\  & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

so the other point of intersection is $(\frac{1}{4},1).$

Therefore, the points of intersection are $A(-\frac{1}{4},-3)$ and $B(\frac{1}{4},1).$
